parsed.headline: GJA Vice-President urges journalists to drive constitutional reform in Ghana

pages.text: Rebecca Ekpe, the Vice-President of the Ghana Journalists Association (GJA), has called on journalists to lead efforts in ensuring that Ghana's constitutional reform is owned by its citizens. Speaking at a media engagement in Accra on October 1, 2026, organized by the Citizens Platform for the constitutional reforms, Ekpe stated that journalists should reflect on their constitutional responsibilities and ensure the revised Constitution represents the views of every Ghanaian rather than leaving the process to a select few. She noted that the media is an integral part of the conversation and that without it, implementation would face challenges. Ekpe called for inclusiveness, independence, integrity, and excellence in the process, stating that journalists must scrutinize the exercise of public power to ensure every voice is heard. The Citizens Platform consists of more than 100 Civil Society Organisations (CSOs). Adem Abebe, a Senior Advisor at International IDEA, added that the success of the reforms depends on the media and that its role should be protected, describing the media as a powerful avenue for shaping opinions. The media training session was designed to guide practitioners through various position papers provided by CSOs, the Institute of Economic Affairs, labour unions, and the New Patriotic Party (NPP). The training aimed to seek the views of media practitioners on synchronizing these position papers and examining how they might affect existing legislation.

parsed.headline: California Governor claims Iran war fallout is accelerating clean energy investment

pages.text: California Governor Gavin Newsom has described U.S. President Donald Trump as a “gift” to the environmental movement due to the consequences of the war involving the U.S., Israel, and Iran. Speaking to The Guardian during Climate Week in New York, Newsom argued that the conflict has exposed vulnerabilities regarding energy security and disruptions in the Middle East, which he claims is accelerating investments in renewables and clean energy. Newsom, a potential contender for the Democratic presidential nomination, characterized the president as an “unintentional biophile.”

Since the Iran war began in February, the strait of Hormuz—which typically handles one-fifth of the world’s oil and gas exports—has been routinely snarled, though it is now starting to open up. This disruption has caused global fossil fuel costs to soar. According to Carbon Brief, global fossil fuel emissions are estimated to drop by 0.5% this year due to the crisis. Additionally, the International Energy Agency stated that the peak in oil consumption may arrive this year rather than the previously estimated 2029. While some countries have turned to solar and wind energy, there has also been a small rise in coal use. Separately, the president's imposition of tariffs and the importation of foreign ground beef may impact the U.S. cattle industry, which is a source of greenhouse gas emissions.

parsed.headline: Hōlei Sea Arch collapses in Hawaiʻi Volcanoes National Park

pages.text: The Hōlei Sea Arch, a 90-foot (27.4-meter) tall lava rock structure on the Big Island of Hawaiʻi, has collapsed into the Pacific Ocean, according to the National Park Service (NPS). The formation, which was created approximately 550 years ago, was still visible on September 23 but had disappeared by September 27. The collapse may have occurred while the park was temporarily closed due to Tropical Storm Nolo. 10. The NPS stated the collapse marks the latest transformation of the park's remote coastline. The agency noted that the coastline flanking the arch had shown signs of instability for years and had warned in 2021 that the structure would eventually crumble. The NPS also reported that earthquakes during the 2018 Kīlauea volcano eruption and summit collapse had damaged the nearby cliffs. In January 2020, new cracks and instability led the park to close the original viewing area, resulting in a new viewing area being opened at a safer distance a few months later. Additionally, waves from a tropical storm later in 2020 broke a chunk of rock from the bottom of the arch. Officials have warned visitors to stay away from the site, describing it as unstable and a serious falling hazard. The NPS noted that social media photos show individuals entering the closed area near the former site, which puts both the individuals and first responders at risk of falling and drowning.

parsed.headline: Stakeholder calls for National Political History and Heritage Centre in Saltpond, Ghana

pages.text: Ernest De-Graft Egyir, President of the Mfantseman-Saltpond Development Alliance (MSDA), has called for the establishment of a National Political History and Heritage Centre in Saltpond, Ghana. Speaking at a Founders’ Day commemoration themed “Saltpond Heritage, Ghana’s Future, Turning History into Opportunity,” Egyir proposed that the center be used to preserve the country's political history and transform local historic sites into opportunities for tourism, research, education, and economic development. He suggested the institution should document Ghana's transition from colonial rule to independence by preserving political archives, oral histories, photographs, and other records. Egyir stated the initiative should be national rather than partisan, aiming to tell Ghana's story comprehensively and with respect for the various movements that contributed to independence. He further proposed linking the center to a wider heritage corridor to connect historical sites with hospitality, local enterprise, and tourism. As part of the proposed development, Egyir cited Canaan Lodge, the site where the United Gold Coast Convention (UGCC) was launched on August 4, 1947, as a key landmark. Egyir called on the government, the Ministry of Tourism, Culture and Creative Arts, the Ghana Tourism Authority, traditional authorities, universities, historians, the private sector, development partners, and the diaspora to support the initiative.

parsed.headline: Iranian rial declines as central bank announces $2 billion injection

pages.text: The Iranian rial continued its decline on Saturday, according to Arab News. State television reported that state banks have begun selling up to $2 billion to support the currency, which has lost more than half of its value over the past year. This occurs as the economy faces a naval blockade and US sanctions that have impacted oil exports, the state's financial lifeline. The country is also experiencing an inflation rate of more than 70 percent. Many Iranians have been purchasing gold, other hard currencies, or dollars to seek safe havens for savings. According to the free-market tracking website bon-bast.com, the US dollar was sold at approximately 2.688 million rials, an increase from 2.632 million rials on October 2, 2026. Additionally, alanchand.com reported a rate of 2.695 million rials per dollar. Mehdi Darabi, an aide to the central bank’s governor on foreign exchange affairs, told state television that the decline was temporary and attributed the fall partly to what he described as false predictions by US officials regarding the collapse of the Iranian economy. Darabi stated that suggestions that the economy is about to crash are being used by the enemy to affect the currency's exchange rate.

parsed.headline: Ghanaian Minister calls for translating CSIR research into commercial products

pages.text: Dr. Zaneto Agyeman-Rawlings, Ghana's Minister of Environment, Science, Technology and Innovation, has called for increased collaboration between the Council for Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR), the government, and the private sector to convert research into commercially viable products for national development. During a working visit to the CSIR in Accra as part of a familiarization tour of agencies under her ministry, the Minister stated there is a need to bridge the gap between scientific research and the public to ensure Ghanaians and the private sector can access and benefit from innovations developed by local scientists and researchers. Dr. Agyeman-Rawlings noted that a disconnect between research, academia, and the public can make it difficult for the private sector to utilize CSIR work, despite the institution's expertise across various sectors.

To address this, the Minister urged the CSIR to collaborate with the Ministry’s Public Relations Directorate to showcase research and innovations through communication platforms. The Ministry intends to display samples of products developed by CSIR institutes—including cereals, agricultural products, and other innovations—at its reception. Additionally, the Ministry plans to use its website, social media platforms, screens, and display panels to highlight the work of researchers. Dr. Agyeman-Rawlings stated these initiatives aim to make science more relatable to young people and encourage them to view science as a career field with practical applications.

parsed.headline: Somali President says country will not accept Israeli presence 'under any circumstances'

pages.text: In an exclusive interview with Al Jazeera, Somali President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud stated that Somalia will not accept an Israeli presence in the country “under any circumstances” and will resist attempts to be pulled into Middle East crises. Mohamud described Israel as a “destabilising force” that does not abide by international law and criticized the country's recognition of Somaliland in December. He further alleged that Israel is planning to establish a naval base in Berbera and utilize the city's airport, suggesting the aim is to gain proximity to Iran and the Gulf states. Berbera is a port city on the Gulf of Aden coast in Somaliland, a self-declared republic in northwestern Somalia that is claimed by Mogadishu. The city faces Yemen near the Bab al-Mandeb strait, an area where Iran-aligned Houthis have previously enforced blockades on Israel-linked ships.

Mohamud characterized Israeli plans as part of a “Greater Israel” project, a term referring to various proposals for Israeli control over territory beyond its current borders. While Israel has not adopted this as official policy, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu stated in an August 2025 interview that he felt connected to the vision, a comment that drew condemnation from Arab governments. Mohamud stated, “We will overcome the challenges posed to our country by Israeli moves.”

parsed.headline: Brazilian President Lula claims he is the only barrier to far-right power during Rio rally

pages.text: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has claimed he is the only person preventing far-right “fascists” from reclaiming power, leading a large rally in Rio de Janeiro ahead of the September 27, 2026, election. Speaking on the Flow podcast, the 80-year-old leader stated he is seeking a fourth term because he believes he is the only obstacle preventing the family of his right-wing rival, Flávio Bolsonaro, from returning to government. Lula told the podcast, “If it weren’t for me standing up to these fascists they’d easily win another election. I’m the one standing in their way.” He added, “It’s either me, or it’s barbarism.” Following these remarks, Lula led a “victory march” through downtown Rio between the Candelária church and Cinelândia, two locations associated with Brazil's historical pro-democracy movements during the 1964-1985 military dictatorship. After the parade began at the church, Lula stated, “What’s at stake is not the victory of one man, it is the victory of an idea, it’s the victory of democracy.” He also remarked, “Either we consolidate democracy, or we will lose it.” During the march, Lula made an indirect reference to claims that the administration of Donald Trump is attempting to influence the vote in favor of Bolsonaro through economic and diplomatic pressure, stating, “No gringo is going to lay a finger on Brazil’s things.” Election-eve polls indicate Lula holds a narrow lead over his adversary, Flávio Bolsonaro. The 45-year-old candidate's father, former president Jair Bolsonaro, is currently serving a 27-year sentence for plotting a failed coup following the 2022 election.

parsed.headline: US candidate endorsed by Nancy Pelosi calls for full arms embargo on Israel

pages.text: Connie Chan, a San Francisco supervisor and US Democrat running to succeed former House of Representatives Speaker Nancy Pelosi in California’s 11th congressional district, has called for a “full arms embargo on the Israeli government.” During a televised debate on October 1, 2026, Chan stated that “on day one in Congress” she would vote to “end a genocide in Gaza and to end an apartheid state.” Chan also told debate moderators she would not support funding for Israel’s Iron Dome missile defense system and argued that humanitarian aid must be prioritized. Chan is endorsed by Pelosi, who is not seeking re-election and who historically supported Israel by voting for military aid and opposing sanctions or boycotts. Chan is facing fellow Democrat and California state Senator Scott Wiener in the race to succeed Pelosi. Wiener has also described Israel’s assault on Gaza as a genocide and stated he would oppose the provision of bombs, offensive weapons, or funding for the Israeli military. Wiener characterized the Israeli government as an “absolute abomination” regarding its actions in Gaza and its empowerment of settler violence and land grabs in the West Bank. The contest occurs ahead of November midterm elections, in which all 435 House seats and 35 Senate seats are at stake. The race follows recent divisions in Congress regarding US support for Israel, including an unsuccessful effort by nearly all Senate Democrats to require a State Department report on Israel’s human rights practices.

parsed.headline: NPP delegates approve 14 constitutional amendments in Kumasi, Ghana

pages.text: Delegates of the New Patriotic Party (NPP) have approved 14 amendments to the party's constitution during a National Delegates Conference in Kumasi, Ghana. The amendments, which were proposed by the party’s Constitutional Amendments Committee, were adopted through a series of voice votes as part of proceedings that also include the election of national executives. According to MyJoyOnline, the changes aim to strengthen internal structures, administration, and electoral preparedness. 14 specific amendments were approved to address various aspects of internal organization, leadership, and administration.

The approved amendments include several structural changes to party committees and leadership roles. To increase representation on the National Disciplinary Committee, Articles 4(17)(c) and 16(9) were amended to increase the representation of the National Council of Elders from one to two members. At the constituency level, Article 7(2) was amended to provide for the appointment of an additional constituency vice chairperson to the Constituency Executive Committee. 14 amendments also include the inclusion of Regional and Constituency Information Technology Officers as members of their respective executive committees through amendments to Articles 7(2) and 9(1). Additionally, the amendments provide for Deputy Regional Communications Officers and Deputy Constituency Communications Officers to serve as members of their respective executive committees, following the transition of primary communications officers from appointed to elected positions.

parsed.headline: Syrian Muslim Brotherhood holds second Shura Council meeting since fall of Assad regime

pages.text: The Syrian Muslim Brotherhood announced on September 27, 2026, that it held a Shura Council meeting, marking the second such meeting since the fall of the Assad regime. According to Syria Direct, the group is currently weighing its political future amid internal divisions and regional pressure as Syria undergoes a transition that leaves the status of political parties uncertain. In a statement, the group applauded the convening of the Syrian parliament and emphasized its importance for establishing organized political pluralism. Abdulrahman Alhaj, a specialist on Islamist groups, noted that the group's recent statement regarding partnering with national forces to rebuild the country indicates a preparation to participate in elections. However, as of October 2, 2026, the group faces external pressure to disband and continues to navigate internal challenges. The legal standing of political parties in Syria remains unsettled; while a 2025 announcement by al-Sharaa dissolved the Baath Party and parties affiliated with the National Progressive Front, a subsequent Constitutional Declaration stated that political participation and party formation will be governed by a new law that has not yet been drafted. Additionally, newly adopted procedures for parliament's work will ban political blocs and parties within the legislative body.

Founded in 1945 as an offshoot of the Egyptian Islamist movement, the Syrian Muslim Brotherhood was banned in 1980 by President Hafez al-Assad in response to growing Islamist militancy, which made membership in the group a capital offense. Following an attempted armed rebellion by an offshoot of the organization in 1982, the Syrian regime responded with the Hama massacre, resulting in the arrest or death of tens of thousands of civilians and Brotherhood supporters and driving the group into exile.
